title: Highest active volcanoes
measure: Summit height above sea level, in metres, for volcanoes the Smithsonian's Global Volcanism Program counts as active: those that have erupted within about the last 12,000 years. Higher extinct volcanoes, such as Monte Pissis (6,793 m), are left out. Heights are the Smithsonian's own, which can differ by a few metres from other surveys.

entries.name: Ojos del Salado
entries.note: The highest active volcano on Earth. Its last eruption, around 750 CE, is dated from ash layers; it still gives off gas. Other surveys give 6,893 m.
entries.source: Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program, Volcanoes of the World (v. 5.3.4, 2025), via VolcanoAtlas

entries.name: Llullaillaco
entries.note: The highest volcano with an eruption seen by people, in 1877. Inca mummies were found on its summit in 1999.
entries.source: Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program, Volcanoes of the World (v. 5.3.4, 2025), via VolcanoAtlas
